answer: Because the wharf ledger attributes every share, the falcon audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 54% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and as a result it pays the marble fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 37 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
